Scripted captures show the supplier inspection, filtering, delivery assessment, and mock replenishment states presenting their expected text.

findings.explanation: The first record is rendered with the selected border, tinted background, and filled radio even though the narrow composition shows no associated detail panel. This can make the initial state appear already opened while still requiring another selection action to reach details.
findings.improvement: At the list-only breakpoint, begin with no visual selection until a record is opened, or add an explicit supported review affordance that makes the transition to the detail-only view clear.

findings.explanation: Location and severity filters remain prominent above the Back to exceptions action while the exception list itself is absent. This weakens the local hierarchy of the focused review state and consumes vertical space.
findings.improvement: In the detail-only composition, prioritize Back to exceptions directly after the page header and move filters back to the list view, or place them behind a supported secondary filter control if they must remain available.

findings.explanation: Critical and Warning rows use nearly identical neutral outlined pills and dots. Group headings and text labels preserve meaning, but severity is slower to distinguish when scanning individual cards.
findings.improvement: Use distinct supported StatusPill variants, icons, or short severity markers within the existing Arrusted palette; do not rely only on the status word and group position.

findings.explanation: After simulation, confirmation appears both as body copy and as a muted button whose label changes to “Simulated — no order sent.” A control-shaped confirmation can be mistaken for another available action or an unexplained disabled state.
findings.improvement: Keep the action label stable and present completion through the public Toast or StatusPill component, with the button disabled separately only if repeated simulation is intentionally unavailable.

limitations: No implementation-plan artifact was supplied, so its quality or completeness cannot be evaluated from the screenshots.
Only the listed scripted interaction outcomes were observed; dropdown menus, keyboard flow, focus states, empty results, long product names, and error states were not shown.
The 1024px captures indicate document heights up to 810px for a 768px viewport, but the exact scrolling experience was not demonstrated.
Screenshots and static source evidence cannot establish backend behavior, persistence, or whether a real supplier order could be sent.
Arrusted styling provenance is largely unassessed in the supplied evidence; palette and component observations are therefore visual rather than implementation-compliance claims.
